root: ^General Alcino: Well, well. Did you forget how doors work?
^My apologies, General. I should have knocked. The king sent me.

c-0: ^General Alcino: Ah, another of His Majesty's 'special assignments.'
^ Let's see... Perfect. I calculate roughly a two percent chance your recruitment ends in catastrophic loss of life.
^General Alcino: Since you're here, you might as well be useful.
^ Three nights past, we had uninvited guests — a war party of Thorum orcs at the west bridge.
^ Their leader, Drogo, is convinced his precious god Molok speaks to him in dreams.
^General Alcino: Him and his orcs are hunting for something called the Cold Fire Stone — supposedly Molok's prison, if you believe orc bedtime stories.
^Do we have this stone they're looking for?
^General Alcino: That's... complicated. Our elven allies do possess a stone that keeps their forests green year - round and grants them unnaturally long lives,
^General Alcino: Between you and me, it matches every description of this 'Cold Fire Stone.' But then again, zealots are often choosy about facts.
^Then I'll deal with these orcs. Point me toward their camp.
^General Alcino: Easy there, hero. Before you go charging off to single-handedly win my war, we have a more pressing concern.
^ Orcs aren't just brutal — they're cunning.
^General Alcino: Our town library contains records going back centuries. If even one book mentions anything
^ about magical stones or elven artifacts, and those records fall into orcish hands...
^General Alcino: Look, I need someone I can trust to quietly review our archives.
^ Secure anything that might compromise the elve's secret.
^ Can I count on your discretion, recruit? Lives may depend on how well you handle dusty books.
^General Alcino: Good. Off you go, then. To the library.
